case_name: Smt Anitha @ Geetha D/O Arasappa vs Sri M Nagaraja
facts_of_case: The respondent filed a petition for divorce on grounds of cruelty and desertion. The trial court allowed the petition. The appellant is filing this appeal against the trial court's decision.

legal_principles.principle: A party who seeks to establish desertion must show that the other party had a reasonable opportunity to secure them to the matrimonial home.
legal_principles.held: When the respondent contends that the appellant has been residing separately from 23.5.2002, he has filed the case even without making any attempt to secure the appellant to the matrimonial home and having failed to do so, respondent cannot contend that appellant has deserted him.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party alleging cruelty to prove the same.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, he requests the court to set aside the judgment passed by the Family Court and remit the matter to the trial court for fresh consideration.

outcome.final_order: The appeal was allowed, and the trial court's decision was set aside.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for divorce under Hindu Marriage Act
